1.title: Azure RBAC: Roles, Scopes and Access
1.text: Welcome to Module two: Azure R B A C: Roles, Scopes and Access. It covers the exam area Manage Azure identities and governance. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Manage built-in Azure roles. Assign roles at different scopes. Interpret access assignments. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Manage Azure identities and governance (twenty-twenty-five percent). Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft Learn A Z-one hundred four study guide, skills measured as of October twenty-six, two thousand twenty-three.

1.title: What Azure RBAC is
1.text: What Azure R B A C is. Azure role-based access control (Azure R B A C) decides who can do what on which Azure resources. An assignment has three parts. Security principal. Who: a user, group, service principal or managed identity. Role definition. What they can do: a set of permitted actions. Scope. Where: the level at which the role applies.

1.title: What Azure RBAC is, continued
1.text: What Azure R B A C is. The figure shows this: A role assignment: security principal, role definition and scope.

1.title: What Azure RBAC is, continued
1.text: What Azure R B A C is. Do not confuse Azure roles (control access to Azure resources) with Microsoft Entra roles (control access to Entra directory objects, such as Global Administrator, User Administrator).

1.title: Scope and inheritance
1.text: Scope and inheritance. The scope hierarchy, from broad to narrow: management group, subscription, resource group, resource.

1.title: Scope and inheritance, continued
1.text: Scope and inheritance. The figure shows this: Scope hierarchy: management group, subscription, resource group and resource, with inheritance downward.

1.title: Scope and inheritance, continued
1.text: Scope and inheritance. Permissions are inherited downward: a role assigned at the subscription applies to every resource group and resource beneath it. Assign at the narrowest scope that works (least privilege). Exam tip: A role at a higher scope flows down; you cannot remove an inherited role at a lower scope (only change the assignment where it was made).

1.title: Built-in roles
1.text: Built-in roles. Owner. Everything, including assigning roles. Contributor. Create and manage all resources, but not assign roles. Reader. View resources only. User Access Administrator. Manage user access (assign roles) but not manage resources. Resource-specific roles. For example Virtual Machine Contributor, Storage Blob Data Contributor, Network Contributor. A role definition lists Actions (control plane), Not Actions (excluded), and Data Actions (data plane, such as reading blob data). Custom roles can be created when no built-in role fits. Exam tip: "Manage resources but must not assign access" equals Contributor. "Assign access but not manage resources" equals User Access Administrator. "Everything including access" equals Owner.

1.title: Assigning and interpreting access
1.text: Assigning and interpreting access. Assign a role. Access control (I A M) on a scope, Add role assignment, pick the role, the members and the scope. Who has access here? Access control (I A M) greater than Role assignments (shows inherited assignments too). Why does this user have access? Check access shows the user's effective roles and where each comes from. Deny. Deny assignments (created by Azure Blueprints or managed apps) override allows. Permissions are additive: a user with several role assignments gets the union of all permissions. Exam tip: Azure roles control resources; Microsoft Entra roles control the directory. Global Administrator is not an Azure role.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A developer must create and manage virtual machines in one resource group but must not be able to grant access to others. Which role and scope fit best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Virtual Machine Contributor at the resource group. A resource-specific contributor role at the narrowest scope follows least privilege.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A role is assigned at a subscription. What is the effect on a resource group inside it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: The role is inherited by the resource group. Role assignments are inherited by child scopes.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which role can assign roles but cannot manage resources? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: User Access Administrator. User Access Administrator manages access, not resources.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. An administrator wants to see why a user can modify a storage account. Which tool shows the effective roles and their sources? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Check access in Access control (I A M). Check access shows the user's effective permissions and where they come from.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A user is a Reader on a subscription and a Contributor on one resource group. What can the user do in that resource group? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Contribute, because permissions are additive. Permissions from several assignments are combined.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which is a Microsoft Entra role, not an Azure role? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Global Administrator. Global Administrator is an Entra directory role.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What are the three parts of a role assignment? Answer: Security principal, role definition and scope. Question two. What is the scope hierarchy? Answer: Management group, subscription, resource group, resource. Question three. What can Contributor not do? Answer: Assign roles.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does Reader allow? Answer: Viewing resources only. Question five. Are permissions inherited upward or downward? Answer: Downward. Question six. Where do you assign a role? Answer: In Access control (I A M) on the chosen scope.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Assignment: principal plus role plus scope. Scopes: management group, subscription, resource group, resource; inherited downward. Roles: Owner (all plus access), Contributor (resources, no access), Reader, User Access Administrator. Tools: I A M blade, role assignments, check access. Not the same: Azure roles versus Microsoft Entra roles. If this course is helping you, please subscribe to the channel and hit the bell icon, so you get a notification when the next video is out.
